entities.name: United States
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of most frontier AI labs, chipmakers, and the federal bodies that regulate them.

entities.name: China
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of the leading open-weight labs and the Cyberspace Administration's generative-AI approval regime.

entities.name: Taiwan
entities.summary: Home of TSMC, the sole leading-edge foundry for nearly all frontier AI chips.

entities.name: France
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of Mistral AI, the EU's leading sovereign-AI champion.

entities.name: United Kingdom
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of Google DeepMind's London headquarters and the AI Security Institute.

entities.name: Japan
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of SoftBank Group, a top-tier capital source for frontier AI infrastructure.

entities.name: United Arab Emirates
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of MGX, the sovereign-linked investor co-anchoring frontier AI mega-rounds and infrastructure deals.

entities.name: Saudi Arabia
entities.summary: Gulf state whose sovereign capital is increasingly co-anchoring frontier AI funding and infrastructure.

entities.name: Canada
entities.summary: Home jurisdiction of Mila, a leading academic deep-learning research institute.

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.summary: Creator of GPT and ChatGPT, operating as a capped-profit company controlled by a nonprofit foundation.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.summary: Public benefit corporation and builder of the Claude model family, founded by ex-OpenAI researchers.

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.summary: Alphabet's unified AI research and product lab, headquartered in London, builder of the Gemini model family.

entities.name: xAI
entities.summary: Elon Musk's AI lab and builder of the Grok model family, merged into a shared holding structure with X and now under SpaceX.

entities.name: Meta Superintelligence Labs
entities.summary: Meta's restructured AI division (absorbing FAIR and prior Meta AI product teams) responsible for the Llama model family.

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.summary: Paris-based frontier lab and Europe's leading open-weight and commercial model builder.

entities.name: DeepSeek
entities.summary: Hangzhou-based Chinese lab whose efficient open-weight models reset industry assumptions about training cost.

entities.name: Alibaba
entities.summary: Chinese e-commerce and cloud conglomerate whose Alibaba Cloud unit builds the widely adopted Qwen open-weight model family.

entities.name: Moonshot AI
entities.summary: Chinese lab behind the Kimi model family, competing aggressively on cost and long-context performance.

entities.name: Zhipu AI
entities.summary: Chinese lab behind the GLM model family, rebranded consumer-facing products under the Z.ai name.

entities.name: Baidu
entities.summary: Chinese search giant and longstanding builder of the ERNIE model family.

entities.name: Alphabet Inc.
entities.summary: Google's parent holding company and the corporate owner of Google DeepMind.

entities.name: Meta Platforms
entities.summary: Parent company of Meta Superintelligence Labs and owner of the Llama open-weight ecosystem.

entities.name: Amazon
entities.summary: E-commerce and cloud conglomerate, a major Anthropic investor and builder of the Bedrock/Nova model platform via AWS.

entities.name: Microsoft
entities.summary: OpenAI's largest strategic investor and cloud partner via Azure, and shipper of the Copilot product line.

entities.name: SpaceX
entities.summary: Elon Musk's aerospace company, now the parent holding entity above xAI following 2025-2026 corporate restructuring.

entities.name: Amazon Web Services
entities.summary: Amazon's cloud division, operator of the Bedrock model platform and the Trainium custom-silicon program.

entities.name: Nvidia
entities.summary: Dominant AI accelerator maker and CUDA ecosystem owner whose GPU supply and roadmap pace the industry.

entities.name: AMD
entities.summary: Nvidia's primary GPU challenger, anchored by a multi-year, multi-gigawatt compute partnership with OpenAI.

entities.name: Broadcom
entities.summary: Critical custom-silicon design partner for hyperscaler AI ASICs including Google's TPUs.

entities.name: TSMC
entities.summary: Sole leading-edge foundry for nearly all frontier AI chips, a binding industry-wide supply constraint.

entities.name: Apple
entities.summary: Ships on-device and cloud AI as Apple Intelligence, a comparatively slower-moving frontier participant.

entities.name: SoftBank Group
entities.summary: Japanese conglomerate and major OpenAI investor and compute-infrastructure partner via the Stargate project.

entities.name: Thrive Capital
entities.summary: Josh Kushner's venture firm and one of OpenAI's most concentrated institutional backers.

entities.name: Andreessen Horowitz
entities.summary: Major venture firm with a dedicated AI investment strategy, including a lead role in xAI's funding rounds.

entities.name: Sequoia Capital
entities.summary: Major venture firm with sustained frontier-model investments, including participation in xAI's funding rounds.

entities.name: MGX
entities.summary: Abu Dhabi-based, sovereign-linked investment firm co-anchoring mega-rounds and infrastructure deals for OpenAI and xAI.

entities.name: Hugging Face
entities.summary: The dominant open-model hosting hub and library ecosystem, the de facto distribution layer for open-weight AI.

entities.name: U.S. Department of Commerce
entities.summary: US federal department overseeing NIST and, through it, the government's AI standards and export-control apparatus.

entities.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
entities.summary: US standards body under the Commerce Department that houses the Center for AI Standards and Innovation.

entities.name: Center for AI Standards and Innovation
entities.summary: NIST unit (renamed in 2025 from the US AI Safety Institute) evaluating frontier models with an emphasis on standards and security.

entities.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
entities.summary: Primary US enforcement agency for AI-related consumer-protection and competition actions.

entities.name: European Commission
entities.summary: EU executive body whose European AI Office develops and enforces the EU AI Act's general-purpose-AI obligations.

entities.name: European AI Office
entities.summary: European Commission body that develops guidance for and enforces the EU AI Act's general-purpose-AI obligations.

entities.name: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
entities.summary: UK government department that houses the AI Security Institute as a directorate.

entities.name: UK AI Security Institute
entities.summary: UK government directorate evaluating frontier models for national-security-relevant risks, renamed from the AI Safety Institute in 2025.

entities.name: Cyberspace Administration of China
entities.summary: China's primary AI and internet regulator, responsible for generative-AI service approvals.

entities.name: International AI Safety Institute Network
entities.summary: Coalition of national AI safety and security institutes coordinating frontier-model evaluation, launched from the Bletchley Summit process.

entities.name: METR
entities.summary: Berkeley-based nonprofit running independent capability and dangerous-capability evaluations on frontier models.

entities.name: Epoch AI
entities.summary: San Francisco-based nonprofit tracking compute trends, training-run scale, and frontier-model benchmarking data.

entities.name: Apollo Research
entities.summary: London-based research organization specializing in evaluating frontier models for deceptive alignment and scheming.

entities.name: Allen Institute for AI
entities.summary: Seattle nonprofit lab producing fully open models, datasets, and benchmarks as an alternative to closed frontier labs.

entities.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
entities.summary: Academic policy and research hub best known for the annual AI Index Report.

entities.name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute
entities.summary: The oldest dedicated AI safety research organization, focused on theoretical alignment and existential-risk research.

entities.name: Center for AI Safety
entities.summary: Nonprofit behind the widely signed 2023 statement on AI risk and ongoing benchmark and policy work.

entities.name: EleutherAI
entities.summary: Grassroots nonprofit open-research collective behind GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, Pythia, and the Pile dataset.

entities.name: Mila – Quebec AI Institute
entities.summary: Montreal-based academic AI research institute associated with Yoshua Bengio.
